accepted.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the First Round Table Conference?
o: The Congress participated through Gandhi as its sole representative.
The Congress boycotted it, while the Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, princes and Ambedkar attended.
The Congress attended through Sarojini Naidu and Muhammad Iqbal.
It was attended by 46 delegates after the Communal Award.
accepted.x: The Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference. Representatives of the Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, princely states and Ambedkar attended it.
accepted.tq: Test participation through the strongest conference-specific distinction.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - year, venue, agenda, Congress participation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Round Table Conferences:
1. The First Conference agreed on a federal structure.
2. The Second Conference ended in a deadlock over the minorities question.
3. The Third Conference was attended by the Congress and Jinnah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The First Conference agreed on a federal structure and the Second ended in a deadlock over minorities. The Congress and Jinnah were absent from the Third Conference.
accepted.tq: Find the false participation statement before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - year, venue, agenda, Congress participation

accepted.s: Who chaired all the three Round Table Conferences?
accepted.x: All three Round Table Conferences were chaired by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald.
accepted.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the entire series rather than one conference.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - year, venue, agenda, Congress participation

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to participation in all three Round Table Conferences?
o: B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru
accepted.x: B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru attended all three Round Table Conferences.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair involving participants present at all three conferences.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - year, venue, agenda, Congress participation

accepted.s: The White Paper that followed the Third Round Table Conference ultimately contributed to which enactment?
accepted.x: The White Paper prepared after the Third Round Table Conference ultimately led to the Government of India Act, 1935, enacted on 2 August 1935.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional document to its legislative outcome.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - year, venue, agenda, Congress participation

accepted.s: How many delegates attended the Third Round Table Conference?
accepted.x: The Third Round Table Conference was attended by 46 delegates.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical detail using nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - year, venue, agenda, Congress participation

accepted.s: The Civil Disobedience Movement was resumed in January 1932 immediately after which development?
o: The Third Round Table Conference concluded.
Gandhi was arrested and the Congress was subjected to repression.
The Cripps Mission arrived in India.
accepted.x: After Gandhi returned from the Second Round Table Conference, the movement was resumed in January 1932; Gandhi was arrested, the Congress was banned and repressive ordinances were issued.
accepted.tq: Connect the resumption of a movement with the immediate political response.
accepted.sec: Resumption and final withdrawal of CDM

accepted.s: On which date did firing on satyagrahis take place at Berhampur during the repression of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
accepted.x: Firing on satyagrahis at Berhampur took place on 15 January 1932.
accepted.tq: Use the precise day and month to distinguish repression-related events.
accepted.sec: Resumption and final withdrawal of CDM

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the later phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement is correct?
1. Gandhi was released on 8 May 1933.
2. Mass Civil Disobedience was suspended on 14 July 1933.
3. The movement was formally withdrawn in April 1934.
4. Congress contested the 1934 Central Assembly elections.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Individual satyagraha continued after the suspension of mass action, and the Congress later revived the council-entry line.
accepted.tq: Check each date and the connected political development before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Resumption and final withdrawal of CDM

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme?
accepted.x: The Karachi resolution included civil liberties, universal adult franchise, religious neutrality and free primary education. It did not propose abolition of all provincial legislatures.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the listed civil-liberty and socio-economic measures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was included in the economic programme adopted at the Karachi Session?
accepted.x: The Karachi programme included rent and revenue cuts, debt relief and state control of key industries.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive socio-economic measure among reversed alternatives.

accepted.s: The Karachi Congress Session was held shortly after the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. The Congress leadership at the session
o: withdrew the resolution on Fundamental Rights
celebrated political violence as the official method of struggle
admired their bravery while disapproving of political violence
accepted.x: The Congress admired the courage of the three revolutionaries but disapproved of political violence as a method.
accepted.tq: Separate admiration for individual bravery from endorsement of a method of struggle.

accepted.s:
Which of the following was a term agreed to by Lord Irwin under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
1. Release of non-violent political prisoners
2. Remission of fines and return of unsold lands
3. Permission for salt-making in coastal villages for personal use
4. Commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Irwin agreed to release non-violent political prisoners, remit fines, return unsold lands and permit limited salt-making. He refused to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped term by separating Irwin’s agreements from Gandhi’s demands and refusals.
accepted.sec: Gandhi-Irwin Pact - date, terms, mediators, criticism

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT agreed to by Gandhi under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Withdrawal of ordinances issued in connection with the movement
Suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement
Attendance at the Second Round Table Conference
Negotiation with the Government through the Congress Working Committee’s authorisation
accepted.x: Withdrawal of ordinances was an undertaking by Irwin. Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference; the Congress Working Committee had authorised him to negotiate.
accepted.tq: Identify the term belonging to the opposite side of the agreement.
accepted.sec: Gandhi-Irwin Pact - date, terms, mediators, criticism

accepted.s: Who among the following acted as a mediator in the negotiations leading to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
accepted.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru, M.R. Jayakar and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri acted as mediators in the negotiations.
accepted.tq: Choose the mediator from among participants and officials linked with the conferences.
accepted.sec: Gandhi-Irwin Pact - date, terms, mediators, criticism

accepted.s: Which criticism of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was most directly connected with the execution of Bhagat Singh and his comrades?
o: The Pact postponed the Karachi Session.
The Pact prohibited salt-making in coastal villages.
The Pact failed to secure commutation of their death sentences.
The Pact ended the system of separate electorates.
accepted.x: A major criticism was that the Pact did not secure commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru, causing disillusionment among the youth.
accepted.tq: Match the criticism with the specific unresolved issue.
accepted.sec: Gandhi-Irwin Pact - date, terms, mediators, criticism

accepted.s: The Second Round Table Conference was unique among the three conferences because
o: it was the only conference without any Indian delegates
Gandhi was the only conference attended by him
it was the only conference chaired by Gandhi
it was the only one held outside London
accepted.x: The Second Round Table Conference was the only Round Table Conference attended by Mahatma Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-last comparison to identify the unique conference feature.

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the representation at the Second Round Table Conference?
1. Gandhi was the sole representative of the Congress.
2. Sarojini Naidu represented Indian women.
3. Muhammad Iqbal represented Muslim interests.
4. Madan Mohan Malaviya, Ambedkar, Jinnah and Aga Khan also attended.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the participants associated with the Second Round Table Conference.
accepted.tq: Use the complete participant list while checking the distinction between Congress representation and other representation.

accepted.s: The Second Round Table Conference failed primarily because of disagreement over
o: separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes
the venue of the Third Round Table Conference
accepted.x: The conference ended in a deadlock over separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes. MacDonald subsequently threatened to make a unilateral award.
accepted.tq: Identify the central issue rather than a peripheral conference topic.

accepted.s:
Which of the following Andhra-related developments is associated with the Second Round Table Conference?
1. Bobbili Raja attended it.
2. Mocherla Ramachandra Rao attended it.
3. V.V. Jogayya Pantulu assisted Gandhi.
4. A separate-Andhra resolution was handed to Gandhi there.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Bobbili Raja and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao attended the conference, V.V. Jogayya Pantulu assisted Gandhi, and the separate-Andhra resolution was handed to Gandhi there.
accepted.tq: Treat regional details as independent statements and verify each association.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a principal feature of the Communal Award?
o: It introduced joint electorates without reserved seats.
It provided separate electorates for the depressed classes along with several other communities.
It granted complete provincial autonomy to India.
It abolished separate electorates for Muslims and Sikhs.
accepted.x: The Communal Award provided separate electorates for Muslims, Sikhs, Christians and the depressed classes, among others.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Award’s separate-electorate provision from the later Poona Pact arrangement.

accepted.s: The Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 was signed between
o: B.R. Ambedkar and Madan Mohan Malaviya
accepted.x: The Poona Pact was signed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on behalf of the depressed classes and Madan Mohan Malaviya on behalf of caste Hindus.
accepted.tq: Use the signatories to distinguish the Pact from the Award and the Gandhi-Irwin negotiations.

accepted.s: Which arrangement replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes under the Poona Pact?
o: Joint electorates with 147 reserved provincial seats
Nomination of all representatives by the Governor-General
Joint electorates without any reserved seats
Separate electorates with 71 reserved provincial seats
accepted.x: The Poona Pact dropped separate electorates and provided 147 reserved seats in provincial legislatures within joint electorates. The Communal Award had provided 71 seats.
accepted.tq: Compare the two constitutional arrangements by electorate type and seat allocation.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Poona Pact provided for a share for the depressed classes in the central legislature and civil services.
2. The Pact retained separate electorates for the depressed classes.
3. The Pact is often referred to as the Gandhi-Ambedkar Pact.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Pact provided representation for the depressed classes in the central legislature and civil services and is often called the Gandhi-Ambedkar Pact. It replaced separate electorates with joint electorates.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed statement about separate and joint electorates.

accepted.s: The Karachi resolution is regarded as an important precursor to which portions of the Constitution of India?
o: Part I and the Schedules alone
The provisions relating only to the Union Public Service Commission
Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy
The provisions relating only to emergency powers
accepted.x: The Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme foreshadowed Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy.
accepted.tq: Link a historical resolution with its constitutional legacy.

accepted.s: The Poona Pact is historically associated with the roots of reserved seats represented in the Constitution by
accepted.x: The Poona Pact is regarded as a historical root of the reservation of seats reflected in Articles 330 and 332 of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Match the historical development with the relevant constitutional Articles.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of post-Civil Disobedience Movement Telugu works and authors is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bharat Swarajya Yuddham was written by Jagannadh Shastry, while Navayuga Gandhi was written by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu.
accepted.tq: Use the author-work pair and reject swapped authorship options.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the dates of the Second Round Table Conference is correct?
o: It was held in 1930 and is generally dated to November–December 1932.
It was held in 1931, generally from September to December, although some accounts give November–December 1931.
It was held in 1932 from 17 November to 24 December only.
It was held in 1934 after the final withdrawal of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
accepted.x: The Second Round Table Conference was held in 1931, generally dated September to December; some accounts specify November–December 1931. The 1932 dating is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Resolve the close-date confusion by fixing the conference to the correct year.
